docs.title: Vector API Reference
docs.text: The Vector API provides comprehensive tools for creating and manipulating 2D and 3D vectors. These APIs are essential for geometric calculations, physics simulations, and spatial transformations.

docs.title: Vector2D
docs.text:
A 2D vector represents a point or direction in two-dimensional space with X and Y coordinates.

Creates a new 2D vector instance.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• x (number): The X coordinate.
  • y (number): The Y coordinate.

docs.title: Returns Vector2D
docs.text: • A new Vector2D object.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4) -- (1)!
  1. Creates a vector at position (3, 4).

Checks if this vector is equal to another vector.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • otherVector (Vector2D): Another vector to compare.

docs.title: Returns boolean
docs.text: • True if both X and Y components are equal.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 2)
local b = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 2)
print(a:IsEqualTo(b)) -- (1)!
  1. Prints true since both vectors have identical coordinates.

Returns the X and Y coordinates of the vector.

docs.title: Returns number, number
docs.text: • The X and Y components.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4)
local x, y = v:GetXY() -- (1)!
  1. Returns x=3, y=4.

Sets the X and Y coordinates of the vector.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• x (number): The new X coordinate.
  • y (number): The new Y coordinate.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(0, 0)
v:SetXY(5, 6) -- (1)!
  1. Updates the vector to position (5, 6).

Scales the vector by a given factor, modifying it in place.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • scalar (number): The multiplier.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(2, 3)
v:ScaleBy(2) -- (1)!
  1. Doubles the vector components: v.x=4, v.y=6.

Divides the vector by a given factor, modifying it in place.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • scalar (number): The divisor.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(4, 6)
v:DivideBy(2) -- (1)!
  1. Halves the vector components: v.x=2, v.y=3.

Adds another vector to this vector, modifying it in place.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • other (Vector2D): The vector to add.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 2)
local b = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4)
a:Add(b) -- (1)!
  1. Vector a now contains (4, 6).

Subtracts another vector from this vector, modifying it in place.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • other (Vector2D): The vector to subtract.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector2D:Create(5, 6)
local b = _A.Vector2D:Create(2, 3)
a:Subtract(b) -- (1)!
  1. Vector a now contains (3, 3).

Computes the 2D cross product (scalar) with another vector.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • other (Vector2D): Another vector.

docs.title: Returns number
docs.text: • The scalar cross product (x₁y₂ - y₁x₂).

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 0)
local b = _A.Vector2D:Create(0, 1)
print(a:Cross(b)) -- (1)!
  1. Prints 1, indicating perpendicular vectors.

Computes the dot product with another vector.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • other (Vector2D): Another vector.

docs.title: Returns number
docs.text: • The dot product.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 2)
local b = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4)
print(a:Dot(b)) -- (1)!
  1. Prints 11 (1×3 + 2×4).

Checks if the vector is zero (0, 0).

docs.title: Returns boolean
docs.text: • True if both X and Y are 0.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(0, 0)
print(v:IsZero()) -- (1)!
  1. Prints true.

Returns the squared length of the vector. More efficient than GetLength when comparing distances.

docs.title: Returns number
docs.text: • Squared magnitude (x² + y²).

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4)
print(v:GetLengthSquared()) -- (1)!
  1. Prints 25 (3² + 4²).

Returns the length (magnitude) of the vector.

docs.title: Returns number
docs.text: • Magnitude √(x² + y²).

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4)
print(v:GetLength()) -- (1)!
  1. Prints 5.

Normalizes the vector to unit length (length = 1), modifying it in place.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4)
v:Normalize() -- (1)!
  1. Vector v now has length 1: v.x=0.6, v.y=0.8.

Returns the angle (in radians) between this vector and another.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • other (Vector2D): Another vector.

docs.title: Returns number
docs.text: • Angle in radians.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 0)
local b = _A.Vector2D:Create(0, 1)
print(a:AngleBetween(b)) -- (1)!
  1. Prints approximately 1.5708 (π/2 radians or 90 degrees).

Rotates the vector by a given angle in radians, modifying it in place.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • rotationRadians (number): The rotation angle in radians.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 0)
v:RotateDirection(math.pi/2) -- (1)!
  1. Rotates the vector 90 degrees: v.x≈0, v.y≈1.

Returns a clone of the vector.

docs.title: Returns Vector2D
docs.text: • A new vector with the same X and Y values.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v1 = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4)
local v2 = v1:Clone() -- (1)!
  1. Creates an independent copy of the vector.

docs.title: Vector2D Operators
docs.text:
Vector2D supports standard arithmetic operators for convenient mathematical operations.

Converts the vector to a string representation.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4)
print(v) -- (1)!
  1. Prints Vector2D(3.000, 4.000).

Returns a new vector representing the sum of two vectors.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 2)
local b = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4)
local c = a + b -- (1)!
print(c) -- (2)!
  1. Creates a new vector without modifying a or b.
  2. Prints Vector2D(4.000, 6.000).

Returns a new vector representing the difference of two vectors.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector2D:Create(5, 6)
local b = _A.Vector2D:Create(2, 3)
local c = a - b -- (1)!
print(c) -- (2)!
  1. Creates a new vector: c = (3, 3).
  2. Prints Vector2D(3.000, 3.000).

Returns a new vector scaled by a scalar value.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(2, 3)
local w = v * 2 -- (1)!
print(w) -- (2)!
  1. Doubles the vector components.
  2. Prints Vector2D(4.000, 6.000).

Returns a new vector divided by a scalar value.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(4, 6)
local w = v / 2 -- (1)!
print(w) -- (2)!
  1. Halves the vector components.
  2. Prints Vector2D(2.000, 3.000).

Compares two vectors for equality.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 2)
local b = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 2)
print(a == b) -- (1)!
  1. Prints true since coordinates match.

docs.title: Vector3D
docs.text:
A 3D vector represents a point or direction in three-dimensional space with X, Y, and Z coordinates.

Creates a new 3D vector instance.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• x (number): The X coordinate.
  • y (number): The Y coordinate.
  • z (number): The Z coordinate.

docs.title: Returns Vector3D
docs.text: • A new Vector3D object.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 3) -- (1)!
  1. Creates a vector at position (1, 2, 3).

Checks if this vector is equal to another vector.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • otherVector (Vector3D): Another vector to compare.

docs.title: Returns boolean
docs.text: • True if X, Y, and Z components are equal.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 3)
local b = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 3)
print(a:IsEqualTo(b)) -- (1)!
  1. Prints true since all coordinates match.

Returns the X, Y, and Z coordinates of the vector.

docs.title: Returns number, number, number
docs.text: • The X, Y, and Z components.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:Create(3, 4, 5)
local x, y, z = v:GetXYZ() -- (1)!
  1. Returns x=3, y=4, z=5.

Sets the X, Y, and Z coordinates of the vector.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• x (number): The new X coordinate.
  • y (number): The new Y coordinate.
  • z (number): The new Z coordinate.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:Create(0, 0, 0)
v:SetXYZ(1, 2, 3) -- (1)!
  1. Updates the vector to position (1, 2, 3).

Scales the vector by a given factor, modifying it in place.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • scalar (number): The multiplier.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 3)
v:ScaleBy(2) -- (1)!
  1. Doubles all components: v.x=2, v.y=4, v.z=6.

Divides the vector by a given factor, modifying it in place.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • scalar (number): The divisor.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:Create(2, 4, 6)
v:DivideBy(2) -- (1)!
  1. Halves all components: v.x=1, v.y=2, v.z=3.

Adds another vector to this vector, modifying it in place.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • other (Vector3D): The vector to add.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 3)
local b = _A.Vector3D:Create(4, 5, 6)
a:Add(b) -- (1)!
  1. Vector a now contains (5, 7, 9).

Subtracts another vector from this vector, modifying it in place.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • other (Vector3D): The vector to subtract.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector3D:Create(5, 7, 9)
local b = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 3)
a:Subtract(b) -- (1)!
  1. Vector a now contains (4, 5, 6).

Computes the 3D cross product with another vector, modifying this vector in place.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • other (Vector3D): Another vector.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 0, 0)
local b = _A.Vector3D:Create(0, 1, 0)
a:Cross(b) -- (1)!
  1. Vector a now contains (0, 0, 1), perpendicular to both original vectors.

Computes the dot product with another vector.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • other (Vector3D): Another vector.

docs.title: Returns number
docs.text: • The dot product.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 3)
local b = _A.Vector3D:Create(4, 5, 6)
print(a:Dot(b)) -- (1)!
  1. Prints 32 (1×4 + 2×5 + 3×6).

Returns the squared length of the vector. More efficient than GetLength when comparing distances.

docs.title: Returns number
docs.text: • Squared magnitude (x² + y² + z²).

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 2)
print(v:GetLengthSquared()) -- (1)!
  1. Prints 9 (1² + 2² + 2²).

Returns the length (magnitude) of the vector.

docs.title: Returns number
docs.text: • Magnitude √(x² + y² + z²).

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 2)
print(v:GetLength()) -- (1)!
  1. Prints 3.

Normalizes the vector to unit length (length = 1), modifying it in place.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 2)
v:Normalize() -- (1)!
  1. Vector v now has length 1: v.x≈0.333, v.y≈0.667, v.z≈0.667.

Returns a clone of the vector.

docs.title: Returns Vector3D
docs.text: • A new vector with the same X, Y, and Z values.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v1 = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 3)
local v2 = v1:Clone() -- (1)!
  1. Creates an independent copy of the vector.

Adds two vectors and returns a new Vector3D without modifying the originals.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • other (Vector3D): The vector to add.

docs.title: Returns Vector3D
docs.text: • A new vector representing the sum.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 1, 1)
local b = _A.Vector3D:Create(2, 2, 2)
local c = a:AddVector(b) -- (1)!
print(c:GetXYZ()) -- (2)!
  1. Creates a new vector without modifying a or b.
  2. Prints 3, 3, 3.

Subtracts two vectors and returns a new Vector3D without modifying the originals.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • other (Vector3D): The vector to subtract.

docs.title: Returns Vector3D
docs.text: • A new vector representing the difference.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector3D:Create(3, 3, 3)
local b = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 1, 1)
local c = a:SubtractVector(b) -- (1)!
print(c:GetXYZ()) -- (2)!
  1. Creates a new vector: c = a - b.
  2. Prints 2, 2, 2.

Normalizes the vector and returns a new Vector3D without modifying the original.

docs.title: Returns Vector3D
docs.text: • A new normalized vector with length 1.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 2)
local n = v:NormalizeVector() -- (1)!
print(n:GetLength()) -- (2)!
  1. Original vector v remains unchanged.
  2. Prints 1.

Scales the vector and returns a new Vector3D without modifying the original.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • scalar (number): The multiplier.

docs.title: Returns Vector3D
docs.text: • A new scaled vector.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 2, 3)
local s = v:ScaleVector(2) -- (1)!
print(s:GetXYZ()) -- (2)!
  1. Original vector v remains unchanged.
  2. Prints 2, 4, 6.

Returns a normal vector's coordinates from yaw and pitch angles.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• yaw (number): Rotation around the Z axis in radians.
  • pitch (number): Rotation around the Y axis in radians.

docs.title: Returns number, number, number
docs.text: • The X, Y, Z coordinates of the normal vector.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local x, y, z = _A.Vector3D:NormalFromYawPitch(math.pi/2, 0) -- (1)!
  1. Computes the normal vector pointing in the specified direction.

Returns a Vector3D object from yaw and pitch angles.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• yaw (number): Rotation around the Z axis in radians.
  • pitch (number): Rotation around the Y axis in radians.

docs.title: Returns Vector3D
docs.text: • A new normalized vector pointing in the specified direction.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:NormalVectorFromYawPitch(math.pi/2, 0) -- (1)!
print(v:GetXYZ())
  1. Creates a unit vector from angular coordinates.

Computes yaw and pitch angles from X, Y, Z coordinates.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• x (number): The X coordinate.
  • y (number): The Y coordinate.
  • z (number): The Z coordinate.

docs.title: Returns number, number
docs.text: • The yaw and pitch in radians.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local yaw, pitch = _A.Vector3D:YawPitchFromNormal(1, 0, 0) -- (1)!
  1. Converts Cartesian coordinates to angular representation.

Computes yaw and pitch angles from the vector itself.

docs.title: Returns number, number
docs.text: • The yaw and pitch in radians.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector3D:Create(1, 0, 0)
local yaw, pitch = v:YawPitchFromVector() -- (1)!
  1. Extracts angular information from the vector's direction.

docs.title: Distance Calculation
docs.text:
local pos1 = _A.Vector2D:Create(0, 0)
local pos2 = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4)
local diff = pos2 - pos1
local distance = diff:GetLength()
print(distance) -- (1)!
  1. Prints 5, the distance between the two points.

docs.title: Direction Vector
docs.text:
local from = _A.Vector3D:Create(0, 0, 0)
local to = _A.Vector3D:Create(10, 0, 0)
local direction = to:SubtractVector(from)
direction:Normalize() -- (1)!
  1. Creates a unit vector pointing from from to to.

docs.title: Vector Projection
docs.text:
local a = _A.Vector2D:Create(3, 4)
local b = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 0)
local projection = (a:Dot(b) / b:GetLengthSquared()) * b -- (1)!
  1. Projects vector a onto vector b.

docs.title: Perpendicular Vector (2D)
docs.text:
local v = _A.Vector2D:Create(1, 0)
v:RotateDirection(math.pi/2) -- (1)!
print(v:GetXY()) -- (2)!
  1. Rotates 90 degrees to get perpendicular vector.
  2. Prints approximately 0, 1.

docs.title: Performance Tips
docs.text:
• Use GetLengthSquared() instead of GetLength() when comparing distances to avoid expensive square root calculations.
  • Use in-place methods (Add, Subtract, Normalize) when you don't need to preserve the original vector.
  • Use immutable methods (AddVector, SubtractVector, ScaleVector) when you need to keep the original vector unchanged.
  • Cache frequently used vectors instead of recreating them every frame.

docs.title: How you can contribute
docs.text:
We understand that reporting bugs, raising change requests, as well as engaging in discussions can be time-consuming, which is why we've carefully optimized our issue templates and defined guidelines to improve the overall interaction within the project. We've invested a lot of time and effort into making our issue tracker and discussion board as efficient as possible.

Our goal is to ensure that our documentation, as well as issue tracker and discussion board, are well-structured, easy to navigate, and searchable, so you can find what you need quickly and efficiently. Thus, when you follow our guidelines, we can help you much faster.

In this section, we guide your through our processes.

docs.title: Creating an issue
docs.text:
• Something is not working?

    Report a bug in Apep by creating an issue with a reproduction

    Report a bug

  • Missing information in our docs?

    Report missing information or potential inconsistencies in our documentation

    Report a docs issue

  • Want to submit an idea?

    Propose a change, feature request, or suggest an improvement

    Request a change

  • Have a question or need help?

    Ask a question on our discussion board and get in touch with our community

    Ask a question

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
• Want to create a pull request?

    Learn how to create a comprehensive and useful pull request (PR)

    Create a pull request

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
Before interacting within the project, please take a moment to consider the following questions. By doing so, you can ensure that you are using the correct issue template and that you provide all necessary information when interacting with our community.

Issues, discussions, and comments are forever

Please note that everything you write is permanent and will remain for everyone to read – forever. Therefore, please always be nice and constructive, follow our contribution guidelines, and comply with our Code of Conduct.

docs.title: Before creating an issue
docs.text:
• Are you using the appropriate issue template, or is there another issue template that better fits the context of your request?

  • Have you checked if a similar bug report or change request has already been created, or have you stumbled upon something that might be related?

  • Did your fill out every field as requested and did you provide all additional information we maintainers need to comprehend your request?

docs.title: Before asking a question
docs.text:
• Is the topic a question for our discussion board, or is it a bug report or change request that should better be raised on our issue tracker?

  • Is there an open discussion on the topic of your request? If the answer is yes, does your question match the direction of the discussion, or should you open a new discussion?

  • Did your provide our community with all the necessary information to understand your question and help you quickly, or can you make it easier to help you?

docs.title: Before commenting
docs.text:
• Is your comment relevant to the topic of the current page, post, issue, or discussion, or is it a better idea to create a new issue or discussion?

  • Does your comment add value to the conversation? Is it constructive and respectful to our community and us maintainers? Could you just use a reaction instead?

docs.title: Rights and responsibilities
docs.text: As maintainers, we are entrusted with the responsibility to moderate communication within our community, including the authority to close, remove, reject, or edit issues, discussions, comments, commits, and to block users who do not align with our contribution guidelines and our Code of Conduct. This role requires us to be actively involved in maintaining the integrity and positive atmosphere of our community. Upholding these standards decisively ensures a respectful and inclusive environment for all members.

docs.title: Code of Conduct
docs.text:
Our Code of Conduct outlines the expectation for all community members to treat one another with respect, employing inclusive and welcoming language. Our commitment is to foster a positive and supportive environment, free of inappropriate, offensive, or harmful behavior.

We take any violations seriously and will take appropriate action in response to uphold these values.1

docs.title: Incomplete issues and duplicates
docs.text:
We have invested significant time and effort in the setup of our contribution process, ensuring that we assess the essential requirements for reviewing and responding to issues effectively. Each field in our issue templates is thoughtfully designed to help us fully understand your concerns and the nature of your matter. We encourage all members to utilize the search function before submitting new issues or starting discussions to help avoid duplicates. Your cooperation is crucial in keeping our community's discussions constructive and organized.

  • Mandatory completion of issue templates: We need all of the information required in our issue templates because it ensures that every user and maintainer, regardless of their experience, can understand the content and severity of your bug report or change request.

  • Closing incomplete issues: We reserve the right to close issues lacking essential information, such as but not limited to minimal reproductions or those not adhering to the quality standards and requirements specified in our issue templates. Such issues can be reopened once the missing information has been provided.

  • Handling duplicates: To maintain organized and efficient communication within our issue tracker and discussion board, we reserve the right to close any duplicated issues or lock duplicated discussions. Opening multiple channels to ask the same question or report the same issue across different forums hinders our ability to manage and address community concerns effectively. This approach is vital for efficient time management, as duplicated questions can consume the time of multiple team members simultaneously. Ensuring that each issue or discussion is unique and progresses with new information helps us to maintain focus and support our community.

    We further reserve the right to immediately close discussions or issues that are reopened without providing new information or simply because users have not yet received a response to their issue/question, as the issue is marked as incomplete.

  1. Warning and blocking policy: We've defined clear guidelines on how we proceed with violations:

    1.1. First warning: Users displaying repeated inappropriate, offensive, or harmful behavior will receive a first warning. This warning serves as a formal notice that their behavior is not in alignment with our community standards and Code of Conduct. The first warning is permanent.

    1.2. Second warning and opportunity for resolution: If the behavior persists, a second warning will be issued. Upon receiving the second warning, the user will be given a 5-day period for reflection, during which they are encouraged to publicly explain or apologize for their actions. This period is designed to offer an opportunity for openly clearing out any misunderstanding.

    1.3. Blocking: Should there be no response or improvement in behavior following the second warning, we reserve the right to block the user from the community and repository. Blocking is considered a last resort, used only when absolutely necessary to protect the community's integrity and positive atmosphere.

    Blocking has been an exceptionally rare necessity in our overwhelmingly positive community, highlighting our preference for constructive dialogue and mutual respect. It aims to protect our community members and team. ↩

docs.title: ACTIONS
docs.text: In the world of scripting, an ACTION represents the core command or operation you want to perform. It can be a spell, a function call, a macro, or any other executable unit. Let's dive into the syntax and explore examples to better grasp the flexibility and functionality offered by the ACTION component.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
The basic syntax for an ACTION is encapsulated within curly braces, with three key elements: ACTION, CONDITIONS, and UNIT.

{ACTION, CONDITIONS, UNIT/FAKEUNIT}

Here's a breakdown of each component:

  • ACTION: This is the command or operation you want to execute. It could be the name of a spell, a function call, a macro, an item number, or even a reference to a library.

  • CONDITIONS: These are the criteria that must be met for the action to take place. Conditions ensure that the action is executed under specific circumstances.

  • UNIT/FAKEUNIT: This specifies the target unit for the action. It could be player, target or any other valid unit identifier or FakeUnit.

docs.title: Spell
docs.text:
{"Charge", CONDITIONS, UNIT}

Executes a spell cast. Replace Charge with the desired spell name. The spell will be cast on the specified UNIT when CONDITIONS are met.

docs.title: Function Call
docs.text:
{function()
  _A.CastSpellByName("Mangle", "target")
end, CONDITIONS, UNIT}

For complex actions, use Lua functions. This allows custom logic and multiple operations within a single action.

Example:

{function()
  if UnitHealth("player") < 50 then
    _A.CastSpellByName("Shield Wall", "player")
  end
end, "spell.ready", "player"}

docs.title: Action Modifiers
docs.text: Action modifiers are special prefixes that alter the behavior of how actions are executed. These modifiers provide fine-grained control over spell casting, queueing, and interruption.

docs.title: Clip Action (!)
docs.text:
{"!Pyroblast", CONDITIONS, UNIT}

Forces the action to interrupt the current cast if one exists. Useful for prioritizing high-priority spells over lower-priority ongoing casts.

Example:

{"!Pyroblast", "buff(Hot Streak)", "target"}

This will interrupt any current cast to immediately execute Pyroblast when Hot Streak is active.

docs.title: Cast While Casting (*)
docs.text:
{"*Fire Blast", CONDITIONS, UNIT}

Allows the spell to be cast while casting other spells. Typically used for instant-cast spells that can be weaved during other casts.

Example:

{"*Fire Blast", "spell.ready && target.distance<=40", "target"}

docs.title: No GCD Spell (&)
docs.text:
{"&Blood Fury", CONDITIONS, UNIT}

Marks the action as not triggering the Global Cooldown (GCD). Used for abilities and items that can be used without waiting for or triggering the GCD.

Example:

{"&#trinket1", "buff(Bloodlust)", "player"}

Uses trinket 1 without triggering the GCD, allowing it to be used between other abilities.

docs.title: Queue Spell (>)
docs.text:
{">Frostbolt", CONDITIONS, UNIT}

Queues the spell to be cast next. Useful for ensuring smooth spell queueing and preventing casting delays.

Example:

{">Frostbolt", "!player.moving", "target"}

docs.title: User Macro (/)
docs.text:
{"/cast SpellName", CONDITIONS, UNIT}
{"/use ItemName", CONDITIONS, UNIT}

Executes a WoW macro command. Any valid slash command can be used.

Examples:

{"/cast Charge", CONDITIONS, UNIT}
{"/use 13", CONDITIONS, UNIT}
{"/startattack", "target.exists && target.enemy", "target"}
{"/stopattack", CONDITIONS, UNIT}
{"/stopcasting", "player.moving", nil}

Use /startattack to begin auto-attacking and /stopattack to halt it.

docs.title: User Library (@)
docs.text:
{"@LibraryName.FunctionName(arguments)", CONDITIONS, UNIT}

Executes a registered user library function. Libraries provide reusable functionality across rotations and must be registered using _A.Library:Add() before use.

Examples:

{"@Prot.Use(Health Stones)", "health<50", "player"}
{"@Prot.PickupHS(unit)", CONDITIONS, "objectID(193169)"}
{"@Utils.InterruptTarget()", "target.casting", "target"}

docs.title: Item Usage (#)
docs.text:
{"#12345", CONDITIONS, UNIT}
{"#trinket1", CONDITIONS, UNIT}

Uses an item by ID or equipment slot name. Available slots include: trinket1, trinket2, neck, waist, hands, and other valid equipment slots.

Examples:

{"#trinket1", "cooldown(trinket1)==0", "player"}
{"#110560", nil, "player"}
{"#waist", CONDITIONS, "target.ground"}

For items that require ground targeting (like engineering belt), use .ground suffix on the UNIT parameter.

docs.title: Special Commands (%)
docs.text: Executes special rotation control commands using the % prefix.

docs.title: Pause Rotation
docs.text:
{"%pause", nil}

Temporarily pauses the rotation execution. Useful when specific conditions require stopping all actions.

docs.title: Target Management
docs.text:
{"%target", CONDITIONS, UNIT}

Changes the current target to the specified UNIT.

Example:

{"%target", "ui(autotarget)==1", "focustarget"}

docs.title: Cancel Buffs
docs.text:
{"%cancelbuff(Buff Name)", CONDITIONS, UNIT}

Removes a specific buff from the target. Commonly used to cancel absorb shields or other buffs that may interfere with mechanics.

Examples:

{"%cancelbuff(Power Word: Shield)", CONDITIONS, "player"}
{"%cancelbuff(Divine Shield)", "debuff(Forbearance)", "player"}

docs.title: Combining Modifiers
docs.text:
Multiple modifiers can be combined to create sophisticated action behaviors:

{"!*Fire Blast", CONDITIONS, UNIT}

This action will both interrupt current casts and can be cast while casting other spells.

{"!&#trinket1", "buff(Bloodlust)", "player"}

This will clip the current cast and use trinket 1 without triggering the GCD.

docs.title: Nested Actions
docs.text:
Actions can be nested to create complex conditional structures:

{{
  {"Execute", "health<=20", "target"},
  {"Mortal Strike", "spell.ready", "target"}
}, "player.incombat && target.WarriorMelee"}

The outer condition must be met, then each inner action is evaluated with its own conditions.

docs.title: Multiple Actions with Shared Conditions
docs.text:
{{
  {"Battle Shout", "!buff(Battle Shout).any", "player"},
  {"Commanding Shout", "!buff(Commanding Shout).any", "player"}
}, "ui(shoutslist)>0"}

All actions in the group share the outer condition, reducing redundancy.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: The ACTION component is the backbone of your scripts, providing diverse execution methods from simple spell casting to complex library calls and special commands. Use this documentation as your guide to crafting powerful and efficient scripts for your projects.

docs.title: CONDITIONS
docs.text:
In DSL mode, Apep already comes with many conditions to facilitate the creation of rotations (Less lines of code and more readable), CONDITIONS are the set of rules or criteria that must be met for an action to take place. They provide a way to control when and how an ACTION is executed. Let's dive into the syntax and explore examples to better understand the functionality offered by the CONDITIONS component.

For example this line:

{"Soulstone", "!buff", "player"},

Creates a soulstone on the player if he doesn't have the soulstone buff. buff is a condition and as you may have noticed there are already a lot of predefined ones.

But if you want to create a custom condition, you already have to do it yourself. example:

-- Register a condition named "class".
-- This condition checks if the specified target unit belongs to the expected class.
-- @param target The unit to check for the class.
-- @param expectedClass The expected class name or class ID to compare with.
-- @return `true` if the target unit belongs to the expected class, `false` otherwise.
_A.DSL:Register('class', function (target, expectedClass)
    local class, _, classID = UnitClass(target)
    if tonumber(expectedClass) then
        return tonumber(expectedClass) == classID
    else
        return expectedClass == class
    end
end)

And this is pure lua code.

docs.title: DLS Syntax
docs.text:
The basic syntax for CONDITIONS is encapsulated within curly braces, as part of the ACTION structure. It consists of three key elements: ACTION, CONDITIONS, and UNIT.

{ACTION, CONDITIONS, UNIT/FAKEUNIT}

Here's a breakdown of each component:

  • ACTION: This is the command or operation you want to execute. It could be the name of a spell, a function call, a macro, an item number, or even a reference to a library.

  • CONDITIONS: These are the criteria that must be met for the action to take place. Conditions ensure that the action is executed under specific circumstances.

  • UNIT/FAKEUNIT: This specifies the target unit for the action. It could be player, target or any other valid unit identifier or FakeUnit.

docs.title: DLS Examples
docs.text:
{ACTION, "inmelee && player.buff(Taste for Blood).stack < 3 && spell(Slam).usable", UNIT}

This example represents a conditional spell casting action. Replace the text within the quotation marks with the name of the desired conditions. Define your specific ACTION and UNIT accordingly.

{ACTION, "player.buff(Bloodlust).any", UNIT}

{ACTION, "player.buff(Bloodlust).any || player.buff(Heroism).any", UNIT}

{ACTION, "inmelee && rage > 80", UNIT}

docs.title: AREA
docs.text: • This condition counts the number of enemy units within a specified distance of a target unit.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit around which to count enemies.
  • DISTANCE: The maximum distance within which to count enemies (default is 40).

docs.title: Returns NUMBER
docs.text: • The total number of enemy units within the specified distance of the target unit.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "UNIT.area(20).enemies >= 3", UNIT},

_A.DSL:Get("area.enemies")("UNIT", "20") >= 3

UNIT:AreaEnemies(20) >= 3
  • This condition counts the number of enemy units within a specified range of a target unit.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit around which to count enemies.
  • RANGE: The maximum range within which to count enemies (default is 40).

docs.title: Returns NUMBER
docs.text: • The total number of enemy units within the specified range of the target unit.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "UNIT.area_range(20).enemies >= 3", UNIT},

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit to check for the debuff stacks.
  • NAME: The name or ID of the debuff to check.

docs.title: Returns NUMBER
docs.text: • The number of stacks of the specified debuff on the unit, or 0 if not present.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "UNIT.debuff(Necrotic Rot).stack.any >= 25", UNIT},

_A.DSL:Get("debuff.stack.any")("UNIT", "Necrotic Rot") >= 25

UNIT:DebuffStackAny("Necrotic Rot") >= 25
  • It checks for player-applied debuffs only.

docs.title: debuff.duration
docs.text: debuff.duration || debuff.remains

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit to check for the remaining duration of the debuff.
  • NAME: The name or ID of the debuff to check.

docs.title: Returns NUMBER
docs.text: • The remaining duration of the specified debuff on the unit in seconds, or 0 if not present.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode

UNIT:DebuffDuration("Corruption")
  • It checks for player-applied debuffs only.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit to check for the total duration of the debuff.
  • NAME: The name or ID of the debuff to check.

docs.title: Returns NUMBER
docs.text: • The total duration of the specified debuff on the unit in seconds, or 0 if not present.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "UNIT.debuff(Corruption).totalduration", UNIT},

_A.DSL:Get("debuff.totalduration")("UNIT", "Corruption")

  • This condition checks whether the specified debuff aura on the target unit is refreshable.
  • A debuff is considered refreshable if its remaining duration is less than or equal to 30% of its total duration.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit to check for the refreshability of the debuff.
  • NAME: The name or ID of the debuff to check.

docs.title: Returns BOOL
docs.text: • true if the debuff is refreshable, or false if not or if the debuff is not present.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "UNIT.debuff(Corruption).refreshable", UNIT},

_A.DSL:Get("debuff.refreshable")("UNIT", "Corruption")

UNIT:DebuffRefreshable("Corruption")
  • It checks for all debuff sources, not just player-applied debuffs.

  • This condition checks if the target unit has a debuff with the specified type.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit to check for the debuff with the specified type.

  • debuff_type: The type of debuff to check for.

    "Magic", "Disease", "Poison", "Curse", "Enrage"

docs.title: Returns BOOL
docs.text: • true if the unit has a debuff with the specified type, false otherwise.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:

{ACTION, "UNIT.debuff(Curse).type", UNIT},

_A.DSL:Get("debuff.type")("UNIT", "Curse")

UNIT:DebuffType("Curse")
  • This condition counts the total number of stacks of all debuffs of a specified type on the target unit.
  • Multiple debuff types can be checked by separating them with ||.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit to count the debuff stacks on.

  • debuff_type: The type of debuff to count stacks for.

    "Magic", "Disease", "Poison", "Curse", "Enrage"

docs.title: Returns NUMBER
docs.text: • The total number of stacks of all debuffs of the specified type(s) on the unit.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "UNIT.debuff(Magic || Curse).count.type > 0", UNIT},
-- Counts stacks of all Magic and Curse debuffs.

_A.DSL:Get("debuff.count.type")("UNIT", "Magic || Curse") > 0

UNIT:DebuffCountType("Magic || Curse") > 0
  • This condition checks if a debuff of a specified dispel type on the target unit is within a random time frame (1 to 3 seconds before its expiration) of its duration, making it a candidate for dispelling.
  • It iterates through all debuffs on the target.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit to check for dispellable debuffs.

  • dtype: The dispel type of the debuff to check for.

    "Magic", "Disease", "Poison", "Curse"

docs.title: Returns BOOL
docs.text: • true if a debuff of the specified dispel type is found and its remaining time is less than (total duration - random(1, 3)), false otherwise.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "UNIT.dispelType.atRndTime(Magic)", UNIT},
-- Checks if any Magic debuff is dispellable at a random time.

_A.DSL:Get("dispelType.atRndTime")("UNIT", "Magic")

UNIT:DispelTypeAtRndTime("Magic")

docs.title: DIMINISHED RETURNS
docs.text: This condition checks the diminished returns state for a specific spell on a unit.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit for which to check DR.
  • SPELL: The spell for which to check DR.

docs.title: Returns NUMBER
docs.text: • The diminished state 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0 for the specified spell on the unit, or -1 if not found.

docs.title: State Description
docs.text: State Description 1 Full duration 0.5 Half duration 0.25 Quarter duration 0 Immune

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "dr(Cyclone).state >= 0.5", UNIT},

_A.DSL:Get("dr.state")(_, "Cyclone") >= 0.5

PLAYER:DrState("Cyclone") >= 0.5

dr.timetomax || dr.ttm

This condition calculates the time remaining until the diminished returns for a specific spell on a unit reach their maximum state.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit for which to calculate the time to maximum DR.
  • SPELL: The spell for which to calculate the time to maximum DR.

docs.title: Returns NUMBER
docs.text: • The time remaining in seconds until the diminished returns reach their maximum state 1 (full duration), or -1 if not found.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "dr(Cyclone).timetomax <= 0", UNIT},

_A.DSL:Get("dr.timetomax")(_, "Cyclone") <= 0

PLAYER:DrTimetomax("Cyclone") <= 0

docs.title: ESSENCES
docs.text: • This condition retrieves the rank of a specific essence by name and slot(optional).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• args(string): A string in the format essenceName, slotName or just essenceName.
    • essenceName: The name of the essence to check for rank.
    • slotName: The slot name to check for rank (optional, can be "main" or "passive").

docs.title: Returns NUMBER
docs.text: • The rank of the specified essence in the specified slot.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "essence(Essence of the Focusing Iris, passive).rank >= 2"},

_A.DSL:Get("essence.rank")(_, "The Well of Existence, main") >= 2

PLAYER:EssenceRank("Blood of the Enemy, main") >= 2

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • NAME: The name of the toggle setting to check.

docs.title: Returns BOOL
docs.text:
• true if the toggle is enabled, false otherwise.

    "MasterToggle", "Interrupts", "Cooldowns", "AoE" and "custom_toggles".

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "toggle(AoE)"},

_A.DSL:Get("toggle")(_, "AoE")

PLAYER:Toggle("AoE")

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• KEY: The name of the key in the GUI configuration to check.
  • UI_KEY (optional): The name of the UI element. Defaults to the current combat routine's name.

docs.title: Returns BOOL or STRING or NUMBER
docs.text: • The value associated with the provided key in the GUI configuration.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
local GUI = {
    ...
    {type = "checkbox", text = "Ashamane's Frenzy", key = "ashamane_key", default = true},
    ...
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "ui(ashamane_key)" },
{ACTION, "ui(some_other_key, MyOtherUI)" },

_A.DSL:Get("ui")(_, "ashamane_key")
_A.DSL:Get("ui")(_, "some_other_key,MyOtherUI")

PLAYER:Ui("ashamane_key")
PLAYER:Ui("some_other_key,MyOtherUI")

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: • UNIT: The unit to check. Defaults to "player" if not specified.

docs.title: Returns NUMBER
docs.text: • The time in seconds it will take for the unit's primary resource (e.g., Mana, Rage, Energy) to reach its maximum value, based on current regeneration rate.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "timetomax < 5"},
{ACTION, "target.timetomax > 2"},

_A.DSL:Get("timetomax")() < 5
_A.DSL:Get("timetomax")("target") > 2

PLAYER:Timetomax() < 5
TARGET:Timetomax() > 2
  • This condition calculates the Global Cooldown (GCD) duration for the player's class.
  • Note: The provided code registers GCDRemains, which returns the time remaining on the GCD, not its total duration. The documentation below reflects the actual GCDRemains function.

docs.title: Returns NUMBER
docs.text: • The time remaining on the GCD in seconds. Returns 0 if GCD is not active.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:

docs.title: timeout
docs.text: timeout || to

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit this timeout is associated with. Can be a unit ID or GUID.
  • NAME_XTIME: A string containing NAME,XTIME.
    • NAME: A unique identifier for this specific timeout.
    • XTIME: The time in seconds the timeout will remain active.

docs.title: Returns BOOL
docs.text: • true when first called or while the timeout is active (i.e., less than XTIME seconds have passed). Returns false once XTIME seconds have elapsed since the first call with the given UNIT and NAME. After returning false, the timeout is reset.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "target.to(bloodlust_window, 40)", target}, -- Will be true for 40s after first use, then false.

_A.DSL:Get("timeout")("target", "bloodlust_window,40")

TARGET:Timeout("bloodlust_window,40")
  • This condition resets a specific timeout, allowing it to start fresh the next time it is called.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• UNIT: The unit this timeout is associated with. Can be a unit ID or GUID.
  • NAME: The unique identifier for the timeout to reset.

docs.title: Returns NIL
docs.text: • This condition does not return a value.

docs.title: Example:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
{ACTION, "target.timeout.reset(bloodlust_window)", target},

_A.DSL:Get("timeout.reset")("target", "bloodlust_window")

target:TimeoutReset("bloodlust_window")

docs.title: TALENTS
docs.text:
• This condition checks if the specified talent is active or learned by the player.
    • In modern WoW versions (Mists of Pandaria and later), talents are typically enabled/disabled. This condition returns true if the talent is enabled.
    • In older WoW versions, talents have ranks. This condition returns true if the talent is learned with at least the specified rank.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• ARG:
    • Modern WoW: The name of the talent (e.g., "Avatar") or its column and row as a string (e.g., "3,1").
    • Older WoW: The name of the talent (e.g., "Improved Frostbolt") or the talent name and rank as a string (e.g., "Improved Frostbolt 2").

docs.title: Returns BOOL
docs.text: • true if the talent condition is met, false otherwise.

docs.title: Examples:
docs.text:
DSLLua CodeLua Mode 
-- Modern WoW (by name)
{ACTION, "talent(Avatar)"},
-- Modern WoW (by column, row)
{ACTION, "talent(3,1)"},
-- Older WoW (by name, checks for at least rank 1)
{ACTION, "talent(Improved Frostbolt)"},

docs.title: Object Manager
docs.text:
The Object Manager is a table that contains all the players, units, and objects currently in the game world that are visible to the player. You can access the Object Manager using the _A.OM global variable. There are several sub-tables within the Object Manager that contain units of a specific type.

_A.OM = {
    All = {},
    Enemy = {},
    EnemyCombat = {},
    Friendly = {},
    Roster = {},
    Dead = {},
    Critters = {},
    Object = {},
    GameObject = {},
    DynamicObject = {},
}

docs.title: Object Manager Tables
docs.text: The Object Manager contains the following tables:

docs.title: All
docs.text: • Contains all the units currently in the game world that are visible to the player.

docs.title: Enemy
docs.text: • Contains all the enemy units currently in the game world that are visible to the player.

docs.title: EnemyCombat
docs.text: • Contains all the enemy units currently in combat that are visible to the player.

docs.title: Friendly
docs.text: • Contains all the friendly units currently in the game world that are visible to the player.

docs.title: Roster
docs.text: • Contains all the members of the player's group.

docs.title: Dead
docs.text: • Contains all the dead units currently in the game world that are visible to the player.

docs.title: Critters
docs.text: • Contains all the critters currently in the game world that are visible to the player.

docs.title: Object
docs.text: • Contains all the game objects currently in the game world that are visible to the player.

docs.title: GameObject
docs.text: • Contains all the game objects currently in the game world that are visible to the player.

docs.title: DynamicObject
docs.text:
• Contains all the dynamic objects currently in the game world that are visible to the player.

And for example if you want to iterate the Roster table:

local roster = _A.OM:Get('Roster')

for _,Obj in pairs(roster) do
    print( Obj.key )
    print( Obj.guid )
    print( Obj.name )
    print( Obj:distance() )
    print( Obj:healthRaw() )
    print( Obj:healthMax() )
    print( Obj:health() )
end

docs.title: Object Manager Methods
docs.text: The Object Manager contains the following methods:

docs.title: Get
docs.text:
• Returns a table of units that match the provided condition. For example if you do
local playerObject = _A.OM:Get("Roster")[UnitGUID("player")]

or

local playerObject = _A.OM["Roster"][UnitGUID("player")]

The table containing the player object is assigned to the playerObject variable that way you dont need to iterate to get the player object

docs.title: UNITS
docs.text:
A unit is an object that has a name and a guid. The name can be player, pet, target, mouseover, pettarget, focus, party1, etc.. You can read more about units in the wowwiki.

  • Opposing arena member with index N (1,2,3,4 or 5).
  • The active bosses of the current encounter if available N (1,2,3...,8).
  • The current player's focus target as selected by the /focus command.
  • The unit which the mouse is currently (or was most recently) hovering over.
  • A valid unit token that always refers to no unit. UnitName will return "Unknown, nil" for this UnitID. Use to force a macro to not auto self-cast (/cast [target=none] Healing Wave).
  • The Nth party member excluding the player (1,2,3 or 4).
  • The pet of the Nth party member (N is 1,2,3, or 4).
  • The current player's pet.
  • The current player.
  • The raid member with raidIndex N (1,2,3,...,40).
  • The pet of the raid member with raidIndex N (1,2,3,...,40)
  • The currently targeted unit. May be overridden in macros by unit specified as a value of respective Secure Button attribute.
  • The current player's vehicle.
  • The Nth nameplate (1,2,3,...,40). Cannot be targeted by spells or commands such as /target nameplate1 or /cast [target=nameplate1] Healing Wave.

docs.title:
spectated
  • The Nth spectated unit (1,2,3,...,15) for either Team "a" or "b", such as "spectatedb2" for the second unit on team B. Only present in commentator mode.

spectatedpet
  • The pet of the Nth spectated unit (1,2,3,...,15) for either Team "a" or "b", such as "spectatedpetb2" for the second units' pet on team B. Only present in commentator mode.
FAKEUNITS
docs.text: A fakeunit is a pointer to an ObjectManager object. In World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King (wotlk), we utilize a GUID (globally unique identifier) because in wotlk, a GUID is represented as a hex number. However, in expansions like Legion, a GUID resembles a format such as Creature-0-1465-0-2105-448-000043F59F. Instead of using GUIDs directly, we use the pointer (key) of the object as the identifier, which allows us to perform actions directly on these pointers.

docs.title: What we can do with fakeunits
docs.text:
One of the notable capabilities while using fakeunits is the ability to cast spells. For instance, you could use a format similar to:

DSLLua Mode 
{"%target", "!is(target)", "nearEnemyCb"}

local target = Object("target")
local nearEnemyCb = Object("nearEnemyCb")

if nearEnemyCb and not target then
    nearEnemyCb:target()
end

Here, the unit nearEnemyCb is used to target the near enemy in combat. This signifies that the fakeunit identifies a target object, and the specified action (target the unit, applying a buff, cast a spell etc.) can be executed on it. This flexibility with fakeunits means you can perform various custom actions programmatically on any target represented by these pointers.

docs.title: Create own fakeunit
docs.text: You can create your own fakeunits by using the _A.FakeUnits:Add method. This allows for highly customized unit selections tailored to specific rotation logic.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
The basic syntax for creating a fakeunit is as follows:

_A.FakeUnits:Add('name', function)
  • 'name': A unique string identifier for your fakeunit. You will use this name in your rotations (e.g., needTaunt.cast).
  • function: The Lua function that will be executed to determine the unit. This function should return the GUID of the selected unit, or nil if no suitable unit is found.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
This example demonstrates how to create a set of fakeunits for selecting enemies based on their distance and combat status.

-- A helper function to find an enemy based on criteria.
-- @param num: The index of the enemy to return (e.g., 1 for the closest, 2 for the second closest).
-- @param near: If true, sorts by nearest distance. If false, sorts by farthest.
-- @param inCombat: If true, only considers enemies in combat. If false, considers all enemies.
local function GetEnemy(num, near, inCombat)
    local tempTable = {}
    -- Decide which object list to use: all enemies or only those in combat.
    local tbl = inCombat and _A.OM:Get('EnemyCombat') or _A.OM:Get('Enemy')

    -- Iterate through the list of enemies.
    for _, Obj in pairs(tbl) do
        -- For this example, we only want enemies that are in front of the player.
        if Obj:infront() then
            -- Store the enemy's GUID and distance for sorting.
            tempTable[#tempTable+1] = { guid = Obj.guid, distance = Obj:distance() }
        end
    end

    -- If there's more than one candidate, sort them.
    if #tempTable > 1 then
        -- Sort by distance, ascending (nearest) or descending (farthest).
        table.sort( tempTable, function(a,b) return near and (a.distance < b.distance) or (a.distance > b.distance) end )
    end

    -- Return the GUID of the enemy at the requested index.
    -- If the index is out of bounds, it will return nil.
    return tempTable[num] and tempTable[num].guid
end

-- Register the fakeunits using the helper function.
-- (1) Nearest enemy
_A.FakeUnits:Add('nearEnemy', function(num)
    return GetEnemy(num, true, false)
end)

-- (2) Nearest enemy that is in combat with the Roster
_A.FakeUnits:Add('nearEnemyCb', function(num)
    return GetEnemy(num, true, true)
end)

-- (3) Farthest enemy
_A.FakeUnits:Add('farEnemy', function(num)
    return GetEnemy(num, false, false)
end)

-- (4) Farthest enemy that is in combat with the Roster
_A.FakeUnits:Add('farEnemyCb', function(num)
    return GetEnemy(num, false, true)
end)

docs.title: Advanced Example: needTaunt
docs.text:
This more complex example creates a fakeunit that identifies enemies which require a taunt. It's useful for tank rotations to ensure threat is maintained on all targets.

local _, _A = ... -- Ensure APEP is loaded

-- Registers a "fake unit" named "needTaunt" with the APEP framework.
-- This function identifies enemy combatants that are not currently being tanked by the player
-- and are within range and line of sight of a specified taunt spell.
-- It returns the GUID of the Nth closest such enemy.
_A.FakeUnits:Add("needTaunt", function(targetIndex, tauntSpell)
    local potentialTauntTargets = {}

    -- Iterate through all known enemies.
    for _, enemy in pairs(_A.OM:Get("Enemy")) do
        -- Filter out players and pets to focus on NPC mobs.
        -- Then, check if the enemy is in combat, within spell range, and has line of sight.
        if not enemy.isplayer and not enemy:Ispet() and enemy:Combat() and enemy:spellRange(tauntSpell) and enemy:los() then
            -- Determine if the player is currently the primary threat target for this enemy.
            -- _A.UnitDetailedThreatSituation returns true if the player is tanking, false otherwise.
            local isPlayerTanking = _A.UnitDetailedThreatSituation("player", enemy.guid)
            if not isPlayerTanking then
                -- If the player is not tanking this enemy, add it to our list of potential taunt targets.
                potentialTauntTargets[#potentialTauntTargets + 1] = {
                    guid = enemy.guid,
                    distance = enemy:distance()
                }
            end
        end
    end

    -- If there's more than one potential target, sort them by distance (closest first).
    if #potentialTauntTargets > 1 then
        table.sort(potentialTauntTargets, function(a, b) return a.distance < b.distance end)
    end

    -- Return the GUID of the enemy at the specified index (e.g., 1st, 2nd closest).
    -- If the `targetIndex` is out of bounds (e.g., asking for the 3rd target when only 2 exist),
    -- it will return nil.
    return potentialTauntTargets[targetIndex] and potentialTauntTargets[targetIndex].guid
end)

In this advanced example, the needTaunt fakeunit takes two arguments: - targetIndex: The index of the desired target from the sorted list (e.g., 1 for the closest enemy needing a taunt). - tauntSpell: The spell ID or name of the taunt ability, used to check spellRange.

This allows for very specific and dynamic unit selection, such as casting a taunt on the second closest enemy that is out of the player's threat range: needTaunt(2, 355).cast.
